responses.response: Diagnose this in order. In this workspace `Container_WebUi` is not a defined kind; the valid container kinds are declared in `projects/shared/spec-containers.c4` and include `Container_Webapp`, `Container_Api`, `Container_Spa`, and others. If the `api` element was declared with that bad kind, LikeC4 never creates the element, so `Element not found: api` can be a cascade, not a separate root cause. After fixing the kind, check scope: the template model nests containers under a system, so outside that block you must reference the FQN such as `mySystem.api`, not bare `api`. Practical order: find the `api = ...` declaration, replace the invalid kind, re-validate, then fix any remaining bare references to the correct FQN or move the relationship inside the parent system block.

The break is not a mysterious FQN problem; it is a modeling and layout mismatch. `system -> system.api` uses a parent system and its child container as if they were a runtime interaction, but the actual runtime participants in this repo are relationships like `user -> mySystem.webapp` and `mySystem.webapp -> mySystem.api` from `projects/template/system-model.c4`. Then `rank same user, system.api` adds static-view layout syntax that does not match the block-style rank hints used here (`rank source { ... }`, `rank sink { ... }`), and `user` is not even part of your stated dynamic step. Fix the scenario first by using the real interacting elements, then remove `rank same` from the dynamic view or express layout only with supported syntax in a normal view.

Start by separating the errors. In this repo `sends` is definitely invalid: model relationship types in `projects/shared/spec-global.c4` are `uses`, `calls`, `async`, `reads`, `writes`, and deployment-only types in `projects/shared/spec-deployment.c4` are `http`, `https`, `tcp`, `nfs`, `amqp`, `oidc_saml`, `ldap`, `sql`, `redis`, `smtp`. So `Unknown relationship type: sends` is a real wrong-relationship error, not an FQN side effect. Then diagnose `dataLayer.cache` on its own: find the declaration of `cache`, confirm whether it is nested exactly under `dataLayer`, and if it lives under a higher parent use the full name such as `mySystem.dataLayer.cache`. Also check that `dataLayer` is a real element, not just a visual grouping, and that the `cache` declaration did not fail earlier. Usually the right workflow is: choose the correct defined relationship type first (`calls`, `async`, `reads`, `writes`, etc.), re-validate, then resolve the element path against the actual nesting.

The root cause is duplicated meaning across two levels of the model. In this workspace logical application traffic belongs in `model {}` using the business relationship types from `projects/shared/spec-global.c4`, while `projects/shared/SPEC_CHEATSHEET.md` explicitly says deployment relationships such as `https` are for infrastructure-specific links and normal traffic should be inherited in deployment through `instanceOf`. The clean fix is to model the logical call once, for example `webapp -[calls]-> api` with `technology 'HTTPS'`, and then let the deployed app instances inherit that relationship. Remove the copied deployment app-to-app edge unless it represents a genuinely infrastructure-only link such as proxy-to-VM, load balancer-to-node, backup NFS, or another network path that does not exist as a logical system interaction.
